page: Vultr vbm-8c-132gb is a bare metal server configured with an Intel Xeon 2288G processor built on the x86_64 architecture. This system features 8 physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 3.7 GHz, supported by a 16 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 128.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is provided by a 3840 GB local NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-threaded capabilities, with gzip compression reaching top-tier speeds of 36.22 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression scoring a strong 14.23 GB/sec. Stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics fall within the average range, alongside a Passmark CPU score of 18785.52. While the Passmark memory score ranks in the top tier, uncached large-block memory read and write bandwidths are relatively weak at 29.76 GB/sec and 15.32 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and Redis SET throughput perform at average levels, while LLM inference speeds are average for small models but drop to weak tiers for 7B parameter models.

This bare metal configuration offers high resource density, combining a high-capacity NVMe SSD with a substantial memory footprint. This makes it a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring dedicated physical hardware without virtualization overhead. The server is well-suited for memory-intensive applications, local database hosting, static web serving, and moderate multi-threaded processing tasks.
